# DMC1 (SLES-50358) engine symbol map
# generated by tools/dmc_symtab.py from E:/SLES_503.58
#
# ELF: MIPS R5900, ET_EXEC, entry 0x00100008, 24 sections, 18025 named symbols
# Counts: 4836 global functions, 5288 static functions, 6590 objects, 1311 other
#
# IMPORTANT - what the t_* sections really are
#   The image has sections t_mdview, t_cam, t_light, t_eff_db, t_event,
#   t_scr_at, t_snd, t_flr, t_inf, t_om_set, t_rck, t_sce_at, t_c_main,
#   t_movie. Every one of them is an overlay slot at 0x01F00000 holding
#   only 13 linker markers (_t_xxx_text_start / _bss_end / ...). They do
#   NOT contain the module code: all real symbols have st_shndx = "main".
#   The subsystem below is therefore derived from the name prefix, which
#   is how the original source named things (Pl00* = player part 00,
#   Em01* = enemy 01, Eff* = effects, Flr* = floor, Cam*/Camera* = camera).
#   Domains in PART 0 are a heuristic bucketing of those prefixes and are
#   labelled as such. PART 1 groups are the subsystem token of each name:
#   a leading verb is skipped, so SetEffTexture lands in Eff and
#   GetPlNowLife lands in Pl, which is where they belong.
#
# How to use this as a behaviour checklist
#   Each PART 1 group is one subsystem and enumerates the behaviour the
#   port needs for it:
#     *Init / *Exit   -> lifecycle you must provide
#     *Update / *Main -> per-frame logic to reproduce
#     *Draw / *Render -> presentation
#     *Get / *Set     -> state the rest of the engine reads; keep it
#                        layout-compatible with the original
#   st_value is the original VMA; st_size is the body size in bytes, a
#   rough measure of how much logic a name hides.
